title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
abstract: arXiv:2611.13975v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the nature of expert specialization remains controversial. Reports of domain-associated expert preferences contrast with analyses attributing routing primarily to token identity or syntactic patterns. To clarify these differing accounts, we look beyond expert-level routing to investigate the neuron-level organization of domain-specialized computation using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP), a measure developed for this analysis. Using mixed-domain calibration data, we identify domain-specialized neuron sets with 58-74% overlap across multi-source samples of the same domain, compared with 15-24% across domains. To understand how this organization evolves during training, we trace neuron importance throughout pre-training and post-training across three fully open MoE families. translated_title: 超越专家边界理解混合专家语言模型
translated_abstract: 在混合专家模型中，专家专业化的本质仍然存在争议。关于领域相关专家偏好的报告，与分析将路由主要归因于词元身份或句法模式的研究形成了对立。为了澄清这些不同的观点，我们超越了专家级别的路由，采用一种为此专门开发的方法——路由感知幅度剖析（RAMP）——来研究领域专业化计算在神经元层面的组织方式。使用混合领域校准数据，我们识别出领域专业化的神经元集合：同一领域的多源样本之间重叠率达到58-74%，而跨领域样本之间仅为15-24%。为了理解这种组织结构在训练过程中如何演变，我们在三个完全开源的MoE模型家族中，追踪了整个预训练和后训练过程中的神经元重要性。结果显示，尽管专家级别的重要性相对稳定，神经元重要性在预训练各检查点之间仍持续发生重组。
tldr: 该研究提出路由感知幅度剖析（RAMP）方法，首次揭示MoE模型中领域专业化计算在神经元层面的组织规律（同领域神经元重叠率高达58-74%，远超跨领域的15-24%），并追踪了这种组织在预训练和后训练全过程中的动态演变。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP) to reveal the neuron-level organization of domain-specialized computation in MoE models—showing 58-74% neuron overlap within the same domain versus 15-24% across domains—and traces how this organization dynamically evolves throughout pre-training and post-training.
